name: Antithesis
oneLine: The antithesis to a game is declining the specific role it's trying to provoke - not winning the exchange, not getting even.
whatYouDid: You found the antithesis for Sweetheart ("Yes, honey!" instead of visible irritation) and for Courtroom (handing the case back to the two actual parties instead of ruling on it), then delivered the classic Why Don't You...?/Yes, But... antithesis to end the boss round.
confusion: Antithesis gets mistaken for reprisal - hitting back, winning the argument, delivering a sharper kick than the one you got; that's still playing the game, just from the other corner of the Triangle.

fromBook.quote: You cannot make anyone else stop playing games... but by using Options, you can stay out of game-playing yourself, or get back out of it if you find that you have already gotten in.

expand.definition: Each named game has a specific move that declines the role it's built to provoke, rather than answering in kind - Berne worked these out game by game in Games People Play; TA Today's general version is to catch the opening Con, cross from Adult, and refuse to take the discount being offered.
expand.otherFraming: A related move is disowning the payoff after the fact: if you miss the opening Con and only notice at the Switch, you can still refuse the bad-feeling Payoff and award yourself a good-feeling one instead, for having spotted it.
expand.tryThisToday: Pick one game you know you play, and write down the single line that would be its antithesis - then notice the next time the opening Con shows up, and try saying it.
